Testing a core of j zeros against those lengths gives all four extensions for j=q-1, only the two mixed extensions for j=2q-2, and all but (1,1) for the other eligible seeds. The empty core misses only (1,1). For a bispecial core containing 1, its left 1-extension forces alignment at the start of a block and its right 1-extension forces length -1 modulo q; the invertible block encoding identifies a unique shorter core. The extension pairs complement exactly, so iteration exhausts all the cores. In the minimal-absence implication, the missing pair plus recurrence lets each occurring maximal proper factor be extended on the missing side with the other bit, proving bispeciality. Reversal commutes with T_q; the absent endpoints match; and the surviving seeds have j+1 in [2,2q-1] not divisible by q, making scales disjoint.
